what: One hub repository named main.hub routes agents to the public repositories of the programme
why: agents entering any single repository could not tell where the other kinds of question are answered
alternatives: keep only the prose ecosystem map in glosa

what: Pin by lockfile (commit + blob per referenced file), not by git submodules
why: an agent needs a few files per repository; submodules force whole clones and detached heads; commit + blob anchoring is already the convention in the equation registry's provenance manifests

what: An edge is admitted only with a literal evidence text in a pinned public file; repositories without one are class catalog
why: the hub must claim nothing of its own; a relation nobody can re-verify is an assertion
alternatives: admit only repositories with edges and omit the rest

what: Public repositories only; non-public work is neither named nor masked
why: a public hub describes only what the public repositories state about themselves
alternatives: private hub with the full graph

what: Four routing facts were scattered over three places (equation source policy, ontology canon agent file, prose ecosystem map); the hub quotes them instead of restating them

First independent pre-publication review: NOT READY. Several edges passed the checker on a bare repository name that merely co-occurred; the health route showed no gate; role strings were described as 'no claim'
outcome: the checker accepted evidence that did not state the relation

what: Evidence text must occur exactly once in the pinned file, be at least 12 characters and not be a bare repository name; edges were retyped to the relation their source sentence actually states; one self-asserted edge (hub lineage) was removed
why: a substring test cannot tell a statement from a co-occurrence; uniqueness and phrase length make the quoted sentence the evidence
alternatives: keep loose matches and rely on review alone
line-number anchors (break on any edit upstream)

what: A relation that is only the hub's own opinion is not an edge
becomes_rule: An edge is admitted only with evidence

what: Second independent review: NOT READY. One retyped edge stated the opposite of its source sentence, one edge quoted a concept-lineage aside as a foundation statement, the equation route told agents to run a CLI that fails on a clean clone without a build step, and graph files could steer build and materialize outside the repository
outcome: evidence uniqueness alone does not make a sentence state the relation; pull-request data reached git and the file system unvalidated

what: Owner and host are an allow-list in code; ids and every path are validated in load() before any command; build refuses to write outside the repository; the weak edge was dropped rather than retyped to fit
why: the graph files are the attack surface of a public repository that other agents will run
alternatives: trust reviewers to catch hostile pull requests

what: Proceed to publish after the open items were listed (licence, author address, stale pins, upstream housekeeping)
why: the hub states only what the target repositories already publish; a re-lock follows any upstream change

what: Licence: MIT for code, CC BY 4.0 for graph data and documentation; author address kept identical to the author's other public repositories
why: an all-rights-reserved hub contradicts a README that invites others to run the scripts; the address is already public on the target repositories

what: Third independent review (three reviewers): one edge typed as consuming an artefact the target does not contain; a licence status stated wrongly; safety wording that invited delaying the emergency screen; build could be steered through a symbolic link into a git hook; a pin was never required to be on the default branch; unvalidated lock fields were rendered into agent-facing cards
outcome: reproduced on scratch copies; all fixed and each fix negative-tested

what: A pin must be an ancestor of the public default branch; symbolic links and unexpected executable bits fail the check; every lock field is validated with full-string matching; third-party actions are pinned by commit
why: agents fetch what the hub links, so the lock file is a supply-chain surface

what: Final gate: build deleted files outside the repository through a symlinked nodes directory before its own symlink refusal ran; workspace mode accepted a non-default branch
outcome: reproduced on a copy; every command now refuses to run on a tree that contains a symbolic link, the stale-card delete is confined to nodes/, and both modes require the default branch; exploit re-run: victim file survives

what: The protocol started at 'pick your intent', which means the problem is already framed before any of the programme's discipline applies; one method repository already states the ordering rule the hub lacked (lens-in before analysis, lens-out after)
The lens precedes problem decomposition: a mandatory Step 0 before any route
why: choosing a route is already an interpretation; the human decision is that the readout reading stated in the listed files comes first
alternatives: require a lens-derived hypothesis after routing

what: Step 0 is a LENS node: each facet must be stated by a pinned source file with a checked quotation; the facet label is a close paraphrase kept to the source's own scope; a facet without a source fails the check
why: a hub that writes its own lens becomes a sixth source of doctrine and breaks pointers-only
alternatives: write the lens questions into AGENTS.md
make the lens an ordinary route that agents may skip

what: Agents given Step 0 restate unverified reported claims as facts less often than agents given the same hub without Step 0
falsifier: paired runs on the same tasks show no difference, or a difference in the wrong direction, in the rate of claims restated as facts

what: Independent review of Step 0: four facet labels said more than their sources, one quotation had its scoping words cropped off, the protocol text claimed the hub adds nothing while it added an ordering rule and a deliverable, and free-text fields could inject headings and links into agent-facing pages
outcome: labels rewritten to each source's own scope and wording; the ordering rule is declared as the hub's own decision; rendered free-text fields, ids, axis and class values and edge type names are validated (one printable line, no markup or links); what a field says is still reviewed by hand

what: Make the skills, plugins, MCP servers, APIs and CLIs of the repositories findable from the hub
why: an agent that has found the right repository still has to find the callable thing inside it
alternatives: leave discovery to each repository's README

what: Surfaces are pinned files listed per repository and rendered to SURFACES.md; plugin and marketplace names are verified against the pinned manifest; the hub ships and runs none of them
why: a catalogue that can drift from the manifest sends agents to install commands that fail
alternatives: vendor the skills into the hub

what: The message of commit 2561eaa says 22 surface entries; the graph it commits has 23 (5 plugins, 6 skill files, 2 prompts, 3 MCP servers, 2 API files, 1 static read API, 3 CLIs, 1 package). The files are right; the count in the message was wrong. Published history is not rewritten.
Make the hub simple to operate: adding and removing repositories and registering skills must be easy, and the hub itself must be usable as an MCP server
why: a hub that needs hand-editing of several files per change will not be kept current

what: One repository is one file (node, surfaces, outgoing edges); add / remove / surfaces commands do discovery, pin and render; add is fail-closed on public status and writes a DRAFT catalog node; every change command is all-or-nothing (pin, render, validate, else roll every file back); the MCP server's write tools are off by default and never commit or push
why: removal becomes deleting one file plus references the tool can find; discovery from well-known file names registers skills without hand-copying; a tool that can publish would bypass the review every earlier round proved necessary
alternatives: let the MCP server commit and push

what: Independent review of the add / remove / MCP change: remove could leave a half-changed tree when the removal made another node invalid; add and surfaces could write an entry that failed validation and then blocked every command; add left its file behind when pinning failed; the MCP server died on one malformed line and reported refused writes as success; an edge could carry a foreign source; one README sentence still pointed at the old edge file
outcome: change commands now run in a transaction with rollback; discovery validates before it writes; edges take their source from the file; the server answers malformed input, including bytes that are not UTF-8, and flags refusals as errors; all reproduced cases re-run

what: A pinned path could be a symbolic link in the source repository (git stores it as a blob whose content is a target path, not file content); materialize would check such a link out locally, and an agent reading 'the pinned file' could be redirected outside the repository
outcome: lock now reads the git tree mode of every referenced path and refuses to pin mode 120000 (symlink); reproduced with a fake clone whose AGENTS.md symlinked to /etc/passwd and confirmed the refusal

what: git-failure messages report only the repository's directory name, never the absolute workspace path
why: an absolute local path in an error string is a minor readout of the machine's layout that costs nothing to remove
alternatives: leave the full path (low severity, but avoidable)

what: Merge all 11 pointer pull requests and the glosa branch
why: the back-pointer content had already been reviewed and approved before each PR was opened
alternatives: merge only the ones already CI-green and wait on the rest

what: toledo#44 needed a rebase: main had moved (an unrelated Clay-governance ACK from other concurrent work) and the merge conflicted in CLAY_GOVERNANCE_ACK.json; resolved by writing this PR's own documentation-only ACK (overwrite is the file's normal practice) and re-running the gate (PASS)

finite-readout-acceleration#5 had an unresolved automated review comment: the AGENTS.md rule 'every function in fra.core is registered with a tier' was broader than CONTRIBUTING.md's own scope (closures and audits only; kinds/describe/timed are exempt helpers)
outcome: reworded to name closures and audits and the exempt helpers explicitly, thread resolved, merged

what: glosa's python-unit-tests CI failed on the pointer PR; confirmed the same failure already exists on glosa main at the same commit (registry.py check: 4 unknown spine_stage violations, GLS-2026-005..008) - pre-existing and unrelated to this documentation-only change; filed as morrocwi/glosa#2 rather than fixed here (out of scope, not this repository's schema to correct); glosa's main branch carries no branch protection, so the merge itself was not blocked
Re-lock main.hub to the merged commits: every pinned repository's AGENTS.md now carries the Programme map pointer, verified directly at each new pinned commit before committing
why: the hub's own pins must track the public state it just helped create
alternatives: leave the hub pinned to the pre-merge commits until a separate session updates it
